Review the spec an AI assistant wrote

Source: R/ai_review.R
tfl_ai_review.Rd

Checks what the assistant returned – a study folder its answer was unpacked into (tfl_ai_unpack()), or one file: a workbook holding any of the ARD, table, report and listing specs, a figure design .yml, a report file of the YAML spec – and sorts what it finds by who acts on it:

Usage

tfl_ai_review(
  file,
  toc = NULL,
  adam = NULL,
  others = NULL,
  metadata = NULL,
  write = TRUE,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

file

A study folder of the YAML spec (each report file against the schema; the definition through the workbook's checks, each finding named by its file and key; spec/_assumptions.yml), a spec workbook (.xlsx), a figure design (.yml), or one report of the YAML spec (spec/outputs/<id>.yml: its items against the schema, and its !r where the schema has a form of its own).

toc

The TOC the specs were written from: a tfl_read_toc() result, or a list of its arguments (path, map, sheet, skip). With it, the outputs, titles and footnotes are checked against it.

adam

The study's data (tfl_read_adam()), for the checks against the data; NULL for none.

others

Specs of the same study already read, for the checks across specs when the file holds only some: a list with any of ard (tfl_read_ard_spec()), table (tfl_read_report_spec()) and listing (tfl_read_listing_spec()).

metadata

The study's ADaM metadata (tfl_adam_metadata(), or the kit's 08_adam_metadata.csv read back), for the checks of the names a workbook writes: a dataset or variable it does not have is the AI's to fix (K14, with the nearest names), and so is a code list value that is not among a variable's levels (K15). NULL for none.

write

Write <file>_repair.md and <file>_questions.md next to the file.

overwrite

Write over them if they are there.

Value

A tfl_ai_review: the rows of tfl_review_spec() plus who (ai or human), with attributes file, kinds, assumptions (the assistant's own list), repair and questions (the two texts) and paths (the files written). Invisibly when write = TRUE.

Details

  • the AI: what it can correct from the kit (tflspec_ai_manual()) and the TOC: a sheet or column that is not the spec's, an output that is not the TOC's, a title or footnote that differs from it, (N=86) where (N={n}) belongs, analyses no table uses, a missing _assumptions sheet, and every error and check of the review (tfl_review_spec(), tfl_check_fig_design());

  • the person: what only they can decide – each assumption the assistant listed, each analysis set's flag, each percentage's denominator, each test or model, each fixed order of levels – and the review's items that are set by hand.

The first half is written as a prompt to paste back into the same chat (<file>_repair.md), the second as a checklist the person answers and pastes back (<file>_questions.md), next to the file – a study folder's in the folder, named after it. The kit's rules and who acts on each review rule are inst/review/ai_rules.csv.

See also

tflspec_ai_manual() for the kit the assistant works from.

Examples

# \donttest{
kit <- tflspec_ai_manual(file.path(tempdir(), "kit-review"), overwrite = TRUE)
#> tflspec AI kit: 7 files, 254 KB, in /tmp/RtmpyXS6aV/kit-review
#>   00_START_HERE.md  (  5 KB)
#>   01_tflspec-ai-user-manual.md  ( 78 KB)
#>   02_tflspec-ai-toc-shell-guide.md  ( 38 KB)
#>   03_spec_schema.yml  (104 KB)
#>   04_blank_spec.md  (  5 KB)
#>   05_example_toc_shell.xlsx  ( 14 KB)
#>   06_example_spec.md  ( 10 KB)
#> Attach all files in /tmp/RtmpyXS6aV/kit-review, plus your TOC and shells, and paste the request in 00_START_HERE.md.
# the example's answer, unpacked into a study folder
st <- file.path(tempdir(), "XYZ-001")
tfl_ai_unpack(kit[basename(kit) == "06_example_spec.md"], st, overwrite = TRUE)
r <- tfl_ai_review(st, write = FALSE)
summary(r)
#>        level
#> who     error check hand
#>   ai        0     0    0
#>   human     0     0   20
head(as.data.frame(r)[r$who == "human", c("output_id", "rule", "message")])
#>   output_id rule
#> 1       T-1  K10
#> 2       T-2  K10
#> 3      <NA>  K11
#> 4       T-1  K13
#> 5       T-1  K13
#> 6       T-1  K13
#>                                                           message
#> 1           T-1: the percentages of CAT are of the analysed rows.
#> 2             T-2: the percentages of AE are of the analysis set.
#> 3 The analysis set SAF is the subjects of ADSL with SAFFL == "Y".
#> 4               T-1: TRT01A prints in the order Drug X | Control.
#> 5                     T-1: AGEGR1 prints in the order <65 | >=65.
#> 6                     T-1: SEX prints in the order Male | Female.
# }
